_what: The idea register and the open-question queue, with dates, as data. Both graders print it; audit.py ages it. Edit this file, not the IDEAS list in the graders.

_states.SIGNAL: graded, in the scorecard, consumed by the board
_states.RECORDED: the feature is computed and stored, and NOTHING consumes it. This is the failure mode this repo is prone to -- audit.py ages these and escalates.
_states.TESTED: measured, result is in, no signal came out of it
_states.OPEN: not measurable yet, or not built
_states.CLOSED: measured and closed with evidence; do not relitigate without new data

_dates: recorded = the date the item entered THIS file. Items that predate the register (2026-11-22) carry that date, because earlier dates are not reliable. A stale date is honest about when it was last looked at, which is the point.

ideas.idea: most-bet / most-watched games are where to fade the public -- NOT standalone, but combined with other signals
ideas.where: volume slice runs on all 12 signals; audit.py section 5 now reports it per filter
ideas.note: HIS CORRECTION, 2026-11-22, and it was right. The standalone form is measured and dead: fading the public INVERTS with volume, 52.1% under 1k bets -> 47.4% at 4k+, spreads 4k+ 43.0% / -17.9% on n=114. But I then closed the whole idea on 3 of 12 signals, which is not a test of it. His words: 'maybe it isn't that easy of just fading public but looking at most bet games and fading public w other signals involved as well -- we have many other different signals too.' Re-run across all 12: n-weighted aggregate is FLAT in every market (|z| all under 1.5), so volume is not a blanket conditioner. Per-cell, 9 of 26 signal x market cells rise monotonically with volume against 4.3 expected by chance, 4 fall -- a mild excess on correlated cells. Spread and total disagree in direction for the same signal (rlm_quiet spread lift +1.3 -> +11.8 with volume; total lift -9.0 -> -22.0). STAYS OPEN: the aggregate says no, the per-cell picture is not flat, NFL cannot check it (0 forward cells at n>=30), and everything above is FIT.

ideas.idea: signals that are strict SUBSETS of other signals are graded against the wrong thing
ideas.where: audit.py section 5 computes lift vs parent; the scorecard still grades vs base rate
ideas.note: Found while re-testing volume properly. rlm_quiet fires 523/523 times where follow_move also fires -- 100%, by construction, since both require the line to have moved toward their side. rlm_ratio 477/477. pin_rlm 87.2% inside pin_move. They are FILTERS, not signals, and the comparison that matters is against the parent on the same games. Scored that way rlm_ratio lifts follow_move on CBB totals from 45.5% to 53.6%, ROI -13.1 to +2.6, n=252, z=+2.03 -- a row the base-rate scorecard reports as unremarkable. Also means the project does not have 12 independent signals: 8 pairs agree on side 100% of the time when both fire, so every 'two signals confirm' reading is in many cases one signal counted twice.

ideas.idea: the BOOK'S OWN EXPOSURE -- which side the house needs. Upstream of why a number moves.
ideas.note: Justin shared a Patrick Everson / Prime Sportsbook post 2026-11-22 listing 'Biggest House Needs' (Lions -3.5, Panthers -2.5, Bills -16.5, Raiders +10.5, Giants +5.5) alongside sharp action and public plays. We collect tickets and money -- what BETTORS did. We have never had what the BOOK is holding. A book moves a number to balance its own book, so its liability is upstream of the move we measure; every signal in this system reads the move and infers backwards. HONEST LIMIT: this is not published as a feed. It appears in weekly columns written by people (Everson/Prime, VSIN liability reports, SuperBook). Treat it as a manual cross-check when Justin shares one, not a signal input, unless a structured source turns up. Also unresolved: Everson listed Lions -3.5 under BOTH 'Top Public Plays' and 'Biggest House Needs', which is not consistent under either reading of the term -- do not build on it until the convention is confirmed.

ideas.idea: 'the public' is one book's clientele, not a fact about the world
ideas.where: every public/fade signal reads Action Network book 69 only
ideas.note: MATERIAL LIMIT ON THE WHOLE FADE-THE-PUBLIC THESIS, found 2026-11-22 by cross-checking Justin's Everson post. Prime listed 'Dolphins +16.5' as a top public play while our Action Network data read 60% of tickets on BUFFALO -- the opposite side. Prime listed public on Ravens +2.5 where we read 49/50, no lean at all. rlm, rlm_quiet, rlm_ratio, sharp_gap and the volume slices all define 'the public' as FanDuel's ticket split via Action Network. If two books disagree about which side the public is on, then a fade signal is fading one book's customers, and its record is a statement about that book, not about public money. Nothing in the archive can currently test this because we have only ever had one source of splits.

ideas.idea: the NFL collector dies silently and nothing notices
ideas.where: audit.py section 0 (heartbeat) now checks it; the workflow itself is NOT fixed
ideas.note: DEFECT. `snap` ran every ~10 min then STOPPED 2026-11-23T01:12Z -- fifteen minutes before the MIN@SF kickoff -- so that game has no closing data. Came back 10:56Z, 9.7h gap. Died again, 3h gap. Last run 14:46Z and was 7.6h cold when Monday's card was being built. CBB and NCAAF ran clean every 30 min through all of it, which is exactly why nothing looked wrong. collect.yml is cron '7 * * * *' with timeout-minutes 350, so ~6 runs overlap by design, and `continue-on-error: true` means a failing step never surfaces. Suspected cause is Actions concurrency/queue pressure on NFL Sunday (6 overlapping 5h50m snap jobs plus cbb, ncaaf and the graders), but THIS IS UNVERIFIED -- the Actions API was not reachable from the session that found it. Justin needs to read the Actions tab. A stale feed is the worst failure this project has because downstream it does not look like an error, it looks like a quiet market.

ideas.idea: the cleanest RLM setup of the week lost outright, not just late
ideas.note: Worth keeping because of how it was described at the time. TB +3.5: 81% of tickets on Detroit, Pinnacle moved 6.5 -> 3.5 (three full points), HELD 13.8h, $100,000 limit -- the largest on the board -- and Patrick Everson/Prime independently reported sharp action on Bucs +6.5/+5.5. Every condition in Justin's thesis, plus outside confirmation. Detroit won 31-21. It did not lose by a hook; it lost by ten. Through the day it was repeatedly called 'right side, price gone' -- that framing was wrong. The move being spent and the read being correct are different claims and only the first was supported. A spent move is not evidence the side is right.

questions.q: Does rlm_ratio's lift over follow_move on totals (+8.1 pts, ROI -13.1 to +2.6, n=252, z=+2.03) survive forward?
questions.why: the best-posed result the project has produced, because it is measured against the right denominator -- the parent signal on the same games, not a market base rate. pin_rlm shows the same direction on totals (+5.3 pts, ROI -9.2 to +1.3), which is weak support and not independent of it. FORWARD, 2026-11-22, once the date-field bug was fixed: lift +12.5 pts, ROI -34.8 to -11.0, n=28, z=+1.10. Direction reproduces out of sample. n=28 and z=1.10 are not evidence, but this is the FIRST thing in this project whose direction has held fit-to-forward at all, and note the parent is badly negative forward (34.0%) so part of the lift is the parent being bad.
questions.next: forward only, let n grow. Do not re-cut it in-sample. Watch whether the lift survives the parent improving.

questions.q: Why does rlm_ratio hold forward while rlm_quiet gets worse, when both are Justin's same reverse-movement idea?
questions.why: they are both filters on follow_move and they split cleanly. rlm_ratio (minority tickets + money share at >=1.2x the ticket share + line confirms) forward lift +12.5 on totals. rlm_quiet (minority tickets AND minority money + line confirms) forward lift -18.2 on the same market. The difference between them is the money ratio: rlm_ratio requires the money to be disproportionately heavy on that side, rlm_quiet requires it to be light. Same line confirmation, opposite money condition, opposite result.
questions.next: this is a mechanism question, not a data-cut question. What kind of account moves a number while leaving a light money share behind?

questions.q: Should the scorecard's signal-PAIR rows be dropped for pairs that agree 100% of the time?
questions.why: the pair rows exist on the theory that evidence combines. For follow_move+rlm_quiet, which agree 523/523, nothing combines -- the pair row is the child row with a different name, and both appeared in the forward anomaly list as separate cells with identical 24-61 records.
questions.next: decide whether to drop them or label them nested; either way the anomaly scan already excludes pairs

questions.q: For each of the 4 live signals: what mechanism does it trade against, documented OUTSIDE our archive?
questions.why: a correlation with no mechanism is a hypothesis. The Pinnacle limit/news research was 5 minutes of outside reading and produced two register items. Nothing has been read that way about the other signals.
questions.next: one signal per week of outside reading

questions.q: Does an independent sharp source systematically disagree with follow_move after a number has already travelled?
questions.why: 2026-11-22, Everson/Prime named sharp action on Saints +11.5 and Raiders +10 -- both the OPPOSITE side from our lean, and in both cases our lean came from follow_move chasing a 1-2 point move that had already happened. follow_move is our worst forward signal, mean z -0.76, +0.22 fit to negative forward. The same source CONFIRMED us where the move was still live: sharps took Bucs at +6.5/+5.5 (Pinnacle has since gone to 3.5) and Eagles at +4.5 (now 3.5). Two confirmations where we were early, two contradictions where we were late. That is a mechanism for the follow_move forward number, not a coincidence.
questions.next: log Everson's weekly post against our follow_move calls for the rest of the season. n will be tiny; it is a mechanism check, not a signal test.

questions.q: Why did price gating come back after being closed with evidence, and what stops the next recurrence?
questions.why: On 2026-11-22 the whole NFL card was ranked by FanDuel-vs-Pinnacle edge, two artifacts were built around it, and it was described as 'the only column that does not depend on a signal record'. Price gating is in the brain doc's CLOSED list -- the gap is non-monotonic, being a point WORSE than Pinnacle was the best bucket, and it had already been removed once for cutting plays with no support. Justin caught it the second time too, in nearly the same words. CLAUDE.md lists the closed items but a closed item is a fact to recall, not a check that fires. Day-one evidence was mixed: the four signal-only plays that price gating had excluded went 2-2, and the biggest price play (ARI +15.5, $100k limit) lost.
questions.next: consider making audit.py assert that the current ranking rule is not one of the closed ones -- a closed item that only lives in prose gets re-derived
